findings.claim: README: 'supply invariant, with permit'. status.json permit.main_theorems: 'process_step_all / inv_callsP: top-level messages and finite sequences with permit included'. Read as: sum of balances = totalSupply always holds for the contract.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: Three separate things are proved, and the link between them and the chain is assumed. (1) One frame: a run of CODE from pc 0 that ends with no error keeps Inv (supply_preserved for 21 selectors and any runner, supply_permit for permit and processRunner). (2) One message: process_step_all says a processMessage run of a message whose code is CODE is a GoodCall, a PermitCall, or (on error) leaves the storage of C as it was. (3) inv_callsP is an induction over an abstract list of steps GoodCall | PermitCall | Untouched. The 'other' step is the bare assumption Untouched C S S' := every storage word of C is kept. Nothing proves that a transaction or a block is such a list: calls into the token from inside another contract's frame, the rollback of an outer frame after an inner successful call, transactions to other accounts, fees and creations are all put in 'other' by assumption (Seq.lean doc lines 26 to 29 say so: 'for the other changes it is the assumption of the step'). It is true in fact (the code has no DELEGATECALL, CALLCODE, SELFDESTRUCT or CREATE: opcode scan in check_code.py), but it is not a theorem. Also Inv is only preserved, never established: no theorem about the constructor or about any real state, so 'sum = totalSupply on chain' needs Inv at deployment as an extra premise. status.json 'assumptions' lists the fork, Sep, data size, NoDelegation1 and the top-level lift, but not the Untouched assumption and not the missing base case.

findings.suggested_fix: Say in status.json: 'Inv is preserved by each successful message whose code is CODE; the chain model is a list of such messages plus steps assumed to keep the storage of C; Inv at deployment is not proved'. To close it: use upstream's transaction level lemmas (storage of C changes only through frames with currentTarget = C) to prove Untouched for messages to other code, and add a base case for the state after the constructor.

findings.claim: status.json permit.status: 'proved for EthLib's real runner (processRunner) ... no assumption on the output of the precompile'; ok_permit_real, permit_readable, supply_permit, PermitCall.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: The statements are real and I found no false hypothesis: ok_permit_real takes only the fork window, data size, the selector, hdel, the frame start and a finished run with processRunner; the precompile output is EthLib's own Ecrecover.compute (a real definition, no opaque), read through recoveredWord (0 when the output is not 32 bytes). I read the bytes 2689 to 2893 by hand: address 1, input 128 bytes at fp, output word at fp-32 that the code zeroes first (so 'h450 = 0' is a fact of the bytes), GAS as gas, the 16 byte bubble idiom, then holder check, expiry check, nonce check in that order. They match the theorem. BUT there is no witness: no Lean run of a successful permit exists, so ok_permit_real, permit_readable, supply_permit and every PermitCall step are not shown non-vacuous by a machine. Of the 4 success paths of permitTail (p5, p6, p10, p11) none has a Sanity theorem, while all 26 success paths of the other 18 functions do. Disclosed in status.json permit.not_covered.

findings.claim: supply_<fn>, supply_preserved, supply_permit, the readable theorems of the writers, GoodCall / PermitCall: stated 'under Sep (callKeys message)'.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: All of them are conditional on Sep, which is never discharged anywhere (rg finds no proof of a Sep value). Sep is local and has the right shape: slot 1 is no balance slot (2^160 facts), the balance slot of each of the 3 call keys is unique among 2^160 addresses, and finitely many inequalities between allowance, wards and nonces slots of the call keys. It is not the false global form and I could not derive a contradiction from its fields, but it cannot be proved in Lean either (2^160 keccak values), so there is no machine-checked instance of any supply_* or of a writer's readable theorem. The 26 Sanity witnesses show the path theorems ok_<fn> are non-empty (they use no keccak hypothesis); they do not instantiate supply_* or *_readable. callKeys (caller, arg1 masked, arg2 masked) does cover every key the 11 writers hash: checked against transferFrom, move, pull, push, burn, mint, rely, deny, approve, permit. rely_readable and deny_readable need no Sep. Disclosed in status.json assumptions.
evidence: token-kit/tokens/usdd/UsddVerify/Usdd/Sep.lean:60-74 (structure Sep: total, uniq, allow, ward, nonce)
findings.suggested_fix: Keep, but say in docs/MAP.md that no instance of supply_* is machine-checked and that Sep fails only on a keccak collision or preimage (about 2^-96 per call under the random function view).

findings.claim: status.json assumptions: 'Fork: path specs, ok_, supply, readable from Berlin; Seq from Paris; permit from Paris and before Glamsterdam.'
findings.what_is_actually_proved: True as written, and it means the 'every selector' result is narrow in forks. permit has a supply theorem, a readable theorem and a place in sequences only for paris <= fork < glamsterdam (10 forks of EthLib's list: paris to bpo5). For Berlin up to Paris there is no message level lift for any function (goodCall_process needs hparis because startState touches the target before Paris). From Glamsterdam: supply_preserved and process_step still type-check (only a lower bound) but they are about the one-counter Nat meter, and EthLib runs transactions with StateGasMeter there, so they say nothing about EthLib's real run; permit has no theorem at all. Whether mainnet at the survey block 26386793 is before Glamsterdam was not checked (see not_checked).
findings.suggested_fix: State the window next to the headline ('Paris to BPO5, Nat meter'). Add fork < .glamsterdam to process_step and GoodCall too, or port the StateGasMeter rules.

findings.claim: status.json permit.hypotheses: 'NoDelegation1 fork state ... a fact of the state, true on chain'.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: It is a hypothesis on the start state of every permit step (PermitCall carries NoDelegation1 fork S), not proved for any state and not shown to be kept along CallsP: a sequence with two permits needs it twice, as two separate assumptions. It is satisfiable (any state where address 1 has no code) but no Lean theorem says so. It cannot be dropped: EthLib resolves an EIP-7702 delegation before the precompile check, so with a delegation at address 1 the STATICCALL would run arbitrary code (still static, so it could only change the returned word). It is used from Pectra only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a lemma that NoDelegation1 holds when address 1 has the empty code hash, and one that GoodCall, PermitCall and a message to other code without a 7702 set-code step keep it. Scratch statement noDelegation1_empty in scratch file PermitWitness.lean (not kept).

findings.claim: status.json theorem_counts.sanity_witnesses: 26; Sanity doc: 'every success path of USDD has a concrete run'.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: 26 witnesses, one per success path of 18 functions (8 views, rely, deny, approve, transfer, push, mint, and 3 each for transferFrom, pull, move, burn). Each is a frame level run from pc 0, for every runner and every bound, computed by the kernel with no keccak hypothesis. Not witnessed: permit (USDD-2), name, symbol, version (ro_name, ro_symbol, ro_version have no *_runs theorem), and no witness at the processMessage level (goodCall_process, process_step_all have no instance). Path kinds 'stuck' (static frame at SSTORE) and duplicates of conditions between a stuck path and an ok path are split by message.isStatic, not contradictory. I did not find a path theorem with contradictory hypotheses in the samples I read (rely, transferFrom, permitTail); the 186 pruned branches are decided inside Lean ('have hd' lines with a tactic), not skipped.

findings.what_is_actually_proved: Confirmed from the readable theorems and the bytes, for the owner: (a) mint(usr, wad) needs only wards[caller] == 1 (mint_readable); a ward can mint any amount to any address, the only limits are the overflow of balanceOf[usr] and totalSupply. rely and deny need the same, so any ward can add wards or remove every other ward. The proofs do not say who the wards are on chain (no state was read). (b) burn(usr, wad) needs no ward: caller == usr, or allowance[usr][caller] >= wad; an allowance of 2^256-1 is never reduced (burn_readable, transferFrom_readable). (c) permit is DAI style: allowed != 0 sets allowance to 2^256-1, allowed == 0 sets it to 0; expiry 0 means no expiry; the nonce must equal nonces[holder]. The domain separator is the word of storage slot 5, fixed at construction and not rebuilt from CHAINID (no CHAINID opcode in the code), so a signature is valid on any chain fork that carries the same storage. (d) Dirty inputs are accepted: address arguments are masked, 'allowed' is any nonzero word (the digest uses 0 or 1), v is masked to its low byte. The contract adds no check on s beyond the precompile's (EthLib: v in {27, 28}, r and s in range), so the mirrored signature (n - s, other v) also passes; the nonce stops a replay. (e) No zero address check in transfer, transferFrom, mint; tokens sent to address 0 stay in the sum. (f) Every function reverts on value; no CALL, DELEGATECALL, SELFDESTRUCT or CREATE in the code; the only outside call is the STATICCALL to address 1.
evidence: usdd.dis.txt (audit scratch, not kept) pc 2432-2435 (PUSH1 5, SLOAD), 2720-2722 (PUSH1 0xff AND), 2521-2523 (ISZERO ISZERO)
findings.suggested_fix: None for the proof. For the owner: list the wards on chain; treat the ward keys as full mint authority.
